defect_interactions.interaction_type: κ-carbide particles sheared by planar dislocation band
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: With overaging (625 °C, 192 h), κ-carbide particles are sheared by planar dislocation bands; large size and high-volume fraction of κ-carbide particles lower work hardening capacity compared with short-time aging (<10 h).

interfaces.interface_notes: Decomposition stops at L1₂(SRO) production in low Al-containing steel, while κ precipitation continues to react in high C and Al-containing steel. Fe(Mn)C carbide is commonly observed in low Al-containing steel (<7 wt%); κ precipitation occurs in high Al-containing steel (≥7 wt%).
interfaces.phase_evolution: γ → γ' + γ'' → γ' + L1₂(SRO) → γ + κ (empirical sequence within Mn 12–30 wt%, Al up to 12 wt%, C 0.6–2.0 wt%). For Fe–28Mn–8.5Al–1C–1.2Si low-density steel, κ phase decomposes from the austenite matrix when the cooling rate is slower than -4.4 °C/h.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip induced by SRO; κ-carbide particles are sheared by planar dislocation bands.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Aging of fully austenite and austenite-based duplex Fe–Mn–C–Al steel causes modulation of C and Al within the austenite and stepwise decomposition.

precipitates.distribution: within austenite grains and along grain boundaries; occurs in high Al-containing steel (≥7 wt%)
within austenite grains and along the grain boundary; commonly observed in low Al-containing steel (<7 wt%)

structures.overall_structure: Aging of fully austenite and austenite-based duplex Fe–Mn–C–Al steel causes modulation of C and Al within the austenite and stepwise decomposition, forming κ phase and Fe(Mn)C carbide within austenite grains and along grain boundaries.

unmapped_findings: Overaging treatment (625 °C for 192 h) produces large size and high-volume-fraction κ-carbide particles that are sheared by planar dislocation bands, giving lower work hardening capacity than short-time aging (<10 h) [b0071].
Aging time and temperature play an important role in the wear resistance of Fe–Mn–C–Al low-density steel; suitable aging parameters require further study [b0080].
Aging treatment optimization is needed to find the balance of strength and ductility with κ phase precipitation [b0101].
